world.setting: Mao's China and 1990s Vancouver — spanning the Shanghai Conservatory of Music, Beijing streets during the 1989 Tiananmen Square protests, remote labor and tractor facilities, and quiet immigrant homes in rainy Vancouver where handwritten manuscripts preserve lost lives.
world.register: literary historical fiction — epic polyphony, tragic history, musicology and memory

sparrow.name: Sparrow
sparrow.role: Composer and teacher at the Shanghai Conservatory — gentle, uncompromising musician who carries his unperformed symphonies in silence through exile and political persecution.
sparrow.look: A slender 35-year-old Chinese man with sensitive thoughtful eyes, slightly disheveled dark hair, high cheekbones, wearing a plain buttoned cotton cadre jacket over a fraying white shirt, posture quiet and introspective.

kai.name: Kai
kai.role: Gifted pianist, Marie's father — charming, ambitious, torn by political survival, denouncing friends to survive the Red Guards before succumbing to lifelong guilt.
kai.look: A charismatic 30-year-old Chinese pianist with sharp intense eyes, neat swept-back black hair, lean athletic frame, wearing a crisp dark wool tunic or pressed shirt, carrying an aura of guarded vigilance.

zhuli.name: Zhuli
zhuli.role: Prodigy violinist at the Conservatory — fierce, uncompromising in her devotion to music, broken by public struggle sessions during the Cultural Revolution.
zhuli.look: A graceful 19-year-old Chinese violinist with fiery expressive dark eyes, hair tied back with a simple red ribbon, slender hands calloused from violin strings, wearing a modest dark cotton student dress.

marie.name: Marie
marie.role: Narrator and mathematician in 1990s Vancouver — Kai's daughter who reconstructs her family's erased past through fragments of The Book of Records.
marie.look: A 22-year-old Chinese-Canadian woman with intelligent observant dark eyes, shoulder-length straight black hair, wearing an oversized knit wool sweater and denim, studying handwritten notebooks at a wooden desk.

aiming.name: Ai-ming
aiming.role: Sparrow's daughter and 1989 Tiananmen Square refugee — brings the surviving fragments of The Book of Records to Marie in Vancouver.
aiming.look: A 19-year-old Chinese woman with guarded haunted eyes, chin-length blunt black hair, slender and tense build, wearing a faded olive green military surplus jacket over a dark t-shirt.

room.look: A wood-paneled music practice room in the Shanghai Conservatory with high windows, soundproofed walls, a grand piano, and dusty sunlight streaming across wooden floorboards.

classroom.look: A formal lecture hall and courtyard at the Conservatory, with stone columns, chalkboard, wooden desks, and propaganda banners hung from second-story railings.

street.look: A wide Beijing avenue during the 1989 student demonstrations, crowded with bicycles, makeshift tents, student banners, and towering gray government buildings in the background.

bedroom.look: A modest domestic room in 1990s Vancouver, rain streaking outside the window, bookshelves filled with paper, tea cups, and scattered pages of hand-copied manuscripts on a table.

objects.why: Musical notes, scores, and classical counterpoint representing private human consciousness and forbidden art.
The Book of Records: handwritten notebooks copied and smuggled across generations to preserve identity.
The tragedy of Zhuli and Kai, suicides, and deaths under political violence and erasure.
Burning of musical instruments, classical scores, and cultural artifacts by the Red Guards.
The destruction of 500 pianos at the conservatory and the violent crushing of student protests.
Political repression, totalitarian censorship, and ideological imprisonment.
The political turmoil of the Cultural Revolution and the rainy Vancouver atmosphere.
Shanghai, Beijing, and Vancouver framing the cross-generational migration.
The musical lineage and familial bonds connecting Sparrow, Kai, Zhuli, Ai-ming, and Marie.
The Shanghai Conservatory of Music as the incubator and slaughterhouse of musical genius.

spine.claim: In 1966 Shanghai and 1990s Vancouver, private music and memory become dangerous contraband under state surveillance.
The Cultural Revolution violently dismantles the Shanghai Conservatory, forcing musicians to choose between ideological compromise and fatal defiance.
Zhuli chooses suicide over desecration, Kai lives with devastating complicity, and Sparrow silences his music into a purely mental symphony.
The Book of Records becomes an underground technology of remembrance, resurfacing during the 1989 Tiananmen Square protests.
Marie pieces together the fragmented manuscripts, discovering that memory and music cannot be divided by zero or erased by totalitarian violence.
